line_1.speaker: Sister Odile
line_1.text: The line that asked for morning. Every copy, same hand, very steady. You do not strike a line that steadily unless you have decided the answer is no.

line_2.speaker: Sister Odile
line_2.text: The Hierarch. I did not know the name then. I knew the handwriting, which turns out to be the more useful thing to have known.

line_3.speaker: Sister Odile
line_3.text: A socket. Cleaned. Sized. Whatever sat in it was taken away carefully, and careful is worse than stolen — careful means it was owed to somebody.

gated.speaker: Sister Odile
gated.text: You have stood under the chapel roof. Then you have heard the quiet hour. It is not silence. It is a gap somebody works in.

start.speaker: Sister Odile
start.text: Sister Odile has taken a corner of the tower and made it look lived in, which is more than the tower has managed on its own.

choices.text: I have heard the quiet hour.
Read me what I have been killing.
You have seen the Hierarch's hand.

odile_service.speaker: Odile
odile_service.text: You have looked at enough of them to be worth reading to. They are not monsters in the sense the word is normally used. Each one is a post somebody was assigned and never relieved of. Learn the posting and the fight becomes a conversation.

odile_arc.speaker: Odile
odile_arc.text: The name was struck from every copy and the strokes are all in one hand, and the hand is his. A man does not erase himself out of shame. He does it to keep the account open.
